name: Question 9
problem:
The displacement $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=\frac{4\pi }{3}\,\text{s}.$ Round your final answer to the nearest Newton.
worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate $r$ to get the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =5\cdot ⟨-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-6\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨-20\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,10\operatorname{cos}⁡t-30\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=\frac{4\pi }{3}\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{4\pi }{3}) & =⟨-20\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}),\,10\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})-30\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨10,\,15\sqrt{3}-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of $F(\frac{4\pi }{3})$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|F(\frac{4\pi }{3})| & =\sqrt{(10)^{2}+{(15\sqrt{3}-5)}^{2}} \\  & ≈23\,\text{N}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest Newton.

Question 9
?

The displacement r, in meters, of a particle P of mass 5kg is given by r=⟨4cos⁡t,6sin⁡t−2cos⁡t⟩, where t>0 is the time in seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle when t=4π3s. Round your final answer to the nearest Newton.

a
 14N
b
 19N
c
 31N
d
 23N
e
 29N
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Newton’s second law states that F=ma, where F is the resultant force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we first differentiate r to get the velocity vector:

v=drdt=⟨ddt(4cos⁡t),ddt(6sin⁡t−2cos⁡t)⟩=⟨−4sin⁡t,6cos⁡t+2sin⁡t⟩

Next, we differentiate the velocity vector to get the acceleration vector:

a=dvdt=⟨ddt(−4sin⁡t),ddt(6cos⁡t+2sin⁡t)⟩=⟨−4cos⁡t,2cos⁡t−6sin⁡t⟩

Therefore, the resultant force F at time t equals

F=ma=5⋅⟨−4cos⁡t,2cos⁡t−6sin⁡t⟩=⟨−20cos⁡t,10cos⁡t−30sin⁡t⟩.

When t=4π3s, we have

F(4π3)=⟨−20cos⁡(4π3),10cos⁡(4π3)−30sin⁡(4π3)⟩=⟨10,153−5⟩.

Finally, the magnitude of F(4π3) is given by

|F(4π3)|=(10)2+(153−5)2≈23N

rounded to the nearest Newton.
